Brief rewritten 2026-08-07 — the original approach was wrong for this tree. 🔴 Do not file-copy the DB: (a) task 41's Phase 1 established there is no way to write a file from JS here — no RNFS, no FS TurboModule, op-sqlite gives paths but no write; and (b) a byte-copy of a live SQLite DB is unsafe anyway — with an open WAL it can capture a torn state, which would have been a latent integrity bug even with a filesystem API. What exists is better: op-sqlite's DB object has execute, delete(), attach/detach, getDbPath, loadFile, so the whole ladder is reachable at SQL level with no new native module — VACUUM INTO for an atomic consistent backup, PRAGMA integrity_check, ATTACH + INSERT…SELECT for salvage (which also answers what salvage reads — it skips views and steps past a corrupt table). ✅ VACUUM INTO availability RESOLVED headlessly 2026-08-17 — it is a build fact, not a device fact. The brief said to verify it on device and stop if absent. op-sqlite 17.1.2 compiles its own bundled amalgamation (cpp/sqlite3.c, wired at android/CMakeLists.txt:79) at SQLite 3.51.3, with no SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM/SQLITE_OMIT_ATTACH flags — it does not link Android system SQLite, so the version does not vary by device or OS. 3.51.3 ≫ the 3.27 floor. Phase A can build on it with confidence; Phase B still watches it run, as habit rather than doubt. 🔴 One gap: nothing reports free disk space — attempt-and-catch SQLITE_FULL, setReservedBytes, or a small native call; bring the tradeoff back, since "block before starting" implies knowing in advance. ⚠ backup_log (migration 001) has never been written to or read — 14 is its only natural consumer; use it or retire it. New decisions: do capture logs get backed up (recommend no — they're ephemeral by settled decision, large, and compete for the space the DB needs; task 42's export owns getting them off-device), and the reciprocal of 41's rule that capture degrades where the product DB blocks. Rulings: storage = a new app-owned TurboModule with synchronous append (not react-native-fs — a Promise-based appendFile loses exactly the events before a native crash); twelve streams, one egress class each; crisis stream logs every turn the gate ran on, hit or clear (option (c), reversing the design's own (b) recommendation — a near-miss watch list is also a phrase list and structurally cannot catch the indirect expressions crisis.ts documents itself as missing); actor vocabulary user/coach/system/planner with planner as a sentinel whose expected count is zero (a non-zero count is direct evidence of the unenforced PlanAdjustment contract being violated); in-app thermal/battery sampling built here (Jason's explicit instruction — 🔴 a recorded deviation from orientation §8's pin to task 19, sampling only, no thermal policy); keep everything with a single black-swan ceiling warning and no second trigger; fsync per event for alpha, reverting to boundary-only at beta. ⚠ Four builder calls remain provisional (amendment §8) — the global v is the one that is not cheaply reversible and needs deciding before Phase 2 writes records. Where the frontier is — two threads, and they don't compete

🔴 The corpus collection window is finite, and that reprices everything below. The capture ladder (43) drops free-text conversation capture at open beta — permanently ending the supply of real conversational input that 31's corpus, 38's training data and 40's held-out eval all depend on. The corpus is built during alpha and closed beta, or it is largely not built at all, and every future LoRA iteration and every re-run of the bake-off draws on a corpus whose window has already shut. This is an argument for starting 41 now rather than after the beta-hardening work, and for closed beta being generous with free-text capture while consent and review are still real protections. It is not an argument for extending the window — the mechanism in 43 doesn't bend.

Thread 1 — the strategic one (the model-migration decision). Now 41 → 31 → 38 → 40, then Jason's call. Task 41 is the new front of the chain and it's the move that can happen today: once capture is on, the corpus accumulates while you do everything else, which is the only input on the board that grows without effort. 31's interview and reconstruction work runs in parallel with the capture window rather than waiting on it.

Thread 2 — the tree, then beta hardening. ✅ (a) the three checks on main — done 2026-08-17, green; ✅ (b) push main to GitHub — done. Next: (c) task 37, the live grammar bug, before any alpha capture or the bake-off; then 14 / 15 / 17 / 21 / 32 and the designed visual pass.

✅ 37-before-41 is confirmed and in motion — Jason is running task 37 before task 41 Phase 2 resumes. Sequencing note added 2026-08-17 — 37 before 41, and it is nearly free. Task 37 is a small, headless, no-P grammar fix that is already spike-confirmed (first char [a-zA-Z0-9]; min-length does not work). Task 41 turns on capture, and every capture taken through the unfixed grammar is corpus recorded against a known-defective extractor. Since 41's whole purpose is to feed 31/38/40, landing 37 first costs a few hours and protects the entire corpus window; landing it after means some fraction of the irreplaceable alpha corpus carries a defect the board already knows about. The two do not compete for the same resource — 37 is headless, 41 needs the phone.
